newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Punjab state eyes soybean cultivation.
newsitem.headline: India's Punjab state eyes soybean cultivation.

text.p: India's northern state of Punjab, the country's foodgrains granary, is attempting soybean cultivation as an alternative to rice paddy as part of a diversification of crops, officials said on Monday.
"We have so far introduced contract farming of soybean in four districts of Punjab," said N.S. Brar, executive director of the state-run Punjab Agro Industries Corporation.
Brar told Reuters 1,500 acres has been brought under soybean cultivation and the crop was expected to be ready by October.
Punjab is India's largest producer of wheat and rice.
Farm experts are urging the government to diversify crop patterns since large scale paddy rice cultivation had depleted the state's scarce water resources.
Officials said to motivate the farmers the corporation has distributed high quality soybean seeds and farm implements and fixed a minimum purchase price for soybean.
But Brar said Punjab farmers were lukewarm about shifting from paddy to soybean cultivation.
"There is a competition between soybean and paddy and the Punjab farmer, by choice still prefers paddy because he is convinced that he will earn more," said Brar.
"Most farmers are still not ready to take the risk by totally shifting to soybean from paddy," he said.
Brar said if steps were taken to increase the average yield of soybean to 800 kg per acre from the current 600 kg Punjab farmers would be willing to take up large scale soybean cultivation.
